timeline_summary: Norman Eric Roberts is a 77-year-old male with a complex multisystem disease trajectory spanning 2015-2025. EARLY COURSE (2015-2016): Established cardiovascular disease with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and progressive lumbar spinal stenosis requiring multiple surgeries (2009, 2012, 2016). MID COURSE (2016-2019): Major inflection point with myasthenia gravis diagnosis (positive AChR antibodies 1.52) presenting atypically without ocular/bulbar symptoms. Initial treatment with prednisone (up to 100mg), pyridostigmine, and mycophenolate showed poor response. Concurrent issues included acute angle-closure glaucoma requiring bilateral iridotomy, persistent CK elevation (400-700s), and mild transaminitis. Rituximab initiated October 2019 after IVIG failure. LATER COURSE (2020-2025): Progressive interstitial lung disease with UIP pattern on HRCT, DLCO declining from 62% to 44%. Started nintedanib therapy. Major cardiovascular events in 2024: pulmonary embolism (July), NSTEMI with severe 3-vessel CAD (80% LAD, 99% mid-LAD, 90% circumflex). March 2025 STEMI led to hospice enrollment. ORGAN SYSTEMS: Neurologic (treatment-refractory myasthenia gravis, severe spinal stenosis, peripheral neuropathy), Pulmonary (progressive ILD/fibrosis), Cardiovascular (severe CAD, atrial fibrillation, PE), Hepatic (chronic mild transaminitis, hepatitis B exposure requiring prophylaxis), Musculoskeletal (severe osteoarthritis, multiple fractures). Current terrain dominated by end-stage cardiac disease with multiorgan compromise. Uncertainties include true etiology of weakness (MG vs spinal disease vs deconditioning) and relationship between elevated CK and myasthenia diagnosis.
meds_and_labs_snapshot: Key medications: Rituximab/IVIG for MG (discontinued 2024 after failure), nintedanib for ILD (stopped due to cost), chronic entecavir for HBV prophylaxis, dual antiplatelet post-MI, Pradaxa for PE/AF (discontinued at hospice). Labs show persistent mild anemia (Hgb 8-12), iron deficiency (ferritin 14-18), stable renal function (Cr 0.8-1.2), mild transaminitis (AST/ALT 20-50s range). Post-IVIG hypergammaglobulinemia (IgG 2660-2850). JCV antibody positive (index 3.72). Lipids markedly elevated (LDL 178-236) with statin intolerance. Critical monitoring gaps include limited inflammatory markers and inconsistent autoimmune panels despite complex rheumatologic picture.
